{{one source|date=April 2024}}
In mathematics, a '''minimal K-type''' is a representation of a maximal compact subgroup ''K'' of a [[semisimple Lie group]] ''G'' that is in some sense the smallest representation of ''K'' occurring in a [[Harish-Chandra module]] of ''G''. Minimal K-types were introduced by Vogan<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Vogan |first=David A. |date=January 1979 |title=The Algebraic Structure of the Representations of Semisimple Lie Groups I |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1971266 |journal=The Annals of Mathematics |volume=109 |issue=1 |pages=1–60 |doi=10.2307/1971266|jstor=1971266 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>  as part of an algebraic description of the [[Langlands classification]].
